articles.title: Why is the Trump administration calling bike lanes ‘DEI’? | Dave Schilling
articles.snippet: The government apparently has an issue with paths for cyclists. Take it from someone who can’t ride a bike: this makes no sense I’m out of gas. Not metaphorically. Literally, my car has the barest minimum amount of fuel in it. This is not because I like to live dangerously , a la the great literary hero Austin Powers, but because gas is more expensive than ever. I have nowhere to be today, so I’m allowing my car to sit idle, empty and alone, lest my bank account disappear into the Phantom Zone of negative balance. If things get sticky, I can take public transit or, God forbid, ride a bike. Except I can’t ride a bike, thanks to my parents, who were too busy doing more important tasks than tea
articles.summary: The government apparently has an issue with paths for cyclists. Take it from someone who can’t ride a bike: this makes no sense I’m out of gas.

articles.title: Many professionals take continuing education. Let’s add etiquette classes | Gene Marks
articles.snippet: This type of training is needed now more than ever, as the American workplace gets more and more diverse As a certified public accountant, I’m required to earn at least 80 hours every two years of continuing professional education credits. Many other professions and trades, including lawyers, healthcare professionals, engineers, electricians, plumbers and certain contractors, have similar requirements. It’s a good idea. These professional requirements often also include ethics training. That’s a good idea too. But just getting a refresher on ethics isn’t enough. Something else is needed – something that’s even more important: etiquette. Continue reading...

articles.snippet: Technology is going to drastically reshape the economy, and it’s within our power to decide what that looks like The idea that autonomous, thinking machines may one day destroy property, hierarchy and inequality is as old as western political thought. articles.title: Het rode spook: de opmerkelijke opmars van socialisme in de VS
articles.snippet: Over een dag of 50 kiezen de Amerikanen een nieuw parlement. Sinds Donald Trump II is het politieke landschap in de VS grondig veranderd. De president is onpopulair en het verzet tegen zijn beleid groeit. Bij de oppositie, bij de Democraten, is een strijd bezig voor de ziel van de partij: het gematigde centrum versus progressief-links. Bij de voorverkiezingen wonnen onverwacht veel socialistische kandidaat-Congresleden. Het lijkt op een kleine revolutie. Björn Soenens richt zijn wekelijkse blik dit keer op de socialisten van Amerika.
articles.summary: Over een dag of 50 kiezen de Amerikanen een nieuw parlement. Sinds Donald Trump II is het politieke landschap in de VS grondig veranderd.

articles.title: Live episode: how AI is reshaping our minds – podcast
articles.snippet: In this episode of Science Weekly, recorded in front of an audience at the London podcast festival on 3 September, Ian Sample hears from Michael Safi, the host of the Guardian’s chart-topping podcast about artificial intelligence, Black Box. Hot on the heels of a flurry of cases of artificial intelligence furthering the field , OpenAI declared a major scalp: its latest AI model had cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, a puzzle with a $1m reward that had defied human brains for decades. The achievement bore little resemblance to how mathematical problems normally fall.
